missionVision.text: To document, preserve and share Africa’s cultures, histories, indigenous knowledge and biodiversity through respectful storytelling, so that what our communities know is never lost.
A living archive where every African, at home and in the diaspora, can find the pieces of who they are.

ethics.text: We only record and share what people agree to share.
We credit every voice and share our work back with communities.
We stay, eat, hire and buy locally wherever we go.
We document places without harming the people or land we meet.

founders.name: Naomi
founders.bio: Naomi documents the cultures that live around the land: the beliefs, languages, ceremonies and stories of the communities we visit. [Add a few lines in your own words: who you are and why Gae matters to you.]

founders.name: Jeff
founders.bio: Jeff follows the wildlife and biodiversity in each place we visit, because when an animal or a forest disappears, a piece of our culture goes with it. [Add a few lines in Jeff’s own words.]

journey.text: Close to home: where we learn how to listen and record well.
Where our own identity and roots are.
Every county, every community willing to share.
The rest of the continent, piece by piece.

whyNature.title: Animal totems
whyNature.text: Clans are named for, and bound to, the animals that protect them.

whyNature.title: Hares and hyenas
whyNature.text: Our folktales teach through the creatures we live beside.

whyNature.title: Sacred trees
whyNature.text: Certain trees and groves are places of prayer and gathering.

whyNature.title: Rainmakers
whyNature.text: Those who read the sky, the wind and the birds for the coming season.

whyNature.title: Healers’ plants
whyNature.text: Medicines most of us have never heard of, known by name and use.

whyNatureIntro.title: In Africa, you cannot separate people from the land.
whyNatureIntro.text: When an animal or a forest disappears, a piece of our culture goes with it. So we document both: Jeff follows the wildlife and biodiversity, and Naomi records the cultures that live around them.
whyNatureIntro.hand: a Nat Geo for Africa, told by Africans
